## Mild Heartburn: Common Triggers and What It Usually Means
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

Mild heartburn after dinner for 3 weeks is often related to **acid reflux/GERD**, especially when it happens after meals and there are no alarm symptoms. Common contributors in your situation include **coffee**, **ibuprofen/NSAIDs**, large or late meals, fatty/spicy foods, alcohol, and lying down soon after eating.

## Heartburn Care Plan: Red Flags, Tracking, and Lifestyle Changes
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

### Symptoms that need medical care sooner
Seek prompt medical evaluation if any of these appear:
- **Chest pain**, pressure, or pain spreading to the arm, back, jaw, or shoulder
- **Trouble swallowing** or food getting stuck
- **Vomiting**, especially repeated vomiting or vomiting blood
- **Black stools** or blood in stool
- **Unintentional weight loss**
- Heartburn that becomes **frequent, severe, or wakes you from sleep**
- New shortness of breath, sweating, fainting, or symptoms with exertion
- Symptoms that do not improve after a short trial of lifestyle changes

### 2-week symptom diary template
Use one line per day:
- **Date:**
- **Time heartburn started:**
- **What you ate/drank in the 4 hours before:**
- **Coffee/caffeine:** none / 1 cup / 2+ cups
- **Ibuprofen or other pain reliever:** none / dose and time
- **Body position after dinner:** stayed upright / lay down / bent over
- **Severity (0–10):**
- **How long it lasted:**
- **What helped:**
- **Notes:** stress, late meal, alcohol, exercise, sleep disruption

### Practical diet and behavior suggestions
- Eat **smaller dinners** and avoid very heavy meals late at night.
- Stay **upright for 2–3 hours after eating**.
- Reduce or pause **coffee** for 1–2 weeks to see if symptoms improve.
- Limit common triggers: **fatty/fried foods, spicy foods, chocolate, peppermint, citrus, tomato-based foods, carbonated drinks, and alcohol**.
- Avoid tight belts or clothing after meals.
- If nighttime symptoms happen, try **raising the head of the bed** 6–8 inches.
- Use **ibuprofen less often if possible**; it can irritate the stomach. For headaches, ask a clinician or pharmacist whether a different option is more suitable for you.
- Keep a steady meal schedule and avoid large meals right before bed.
- If symptoms are mild, an over-the-counter **antacid** or **acid reducer** may help short term, but lifestyle changes are the main first step here.

## Two-Week Heartburn Tracking Template
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

- **Days 1–14:** Fill in the diary once daily, plus any extra episode after dinner.
- **Goal:** Identify patterns between meals, coffee, ibuprofen, posture, and symptom severity.
- **Review point:** If symptoms are still happening most days after 2 weeks of changes, schedule a medical visit.

## Sources
- NHS heartburn and acid reflux guidance: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/heartburn-and-acid-reflux/
- MedlinePlus acid reflux information: https://medlineplus.gov/acidreflux.html
- Mayo Clinic GERD overview: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/gerd/symptoms-causes/syc-20361940
